html:
The Tolowa, who call themselves Dee-ni', are an Athabaskan-speaking people of the far north coast of California and the edge of Oregon, around the Smith River and Crescent City. They lived in villages of redwood plank houses, fished salmon and smelt, hunted sea lions and gathered acorns, and held the Nee-dash, a world renewal ceremony. Their neighbours to the south were the Yurok, whose language is unrelated, and inland the Hupa, who speak a related one.

Gold seekers reached their coast in the early 1850s, with the Gold Rush. A massacre at the village of Yontocket around 1853, other killings and disease destroyed most of the people. Survivors were moved for a time to reservations in Oregon and California. Today the Tolowa Dee-ni' Nation is centred at Smith River. See also Athabaskan.
